problem_text:
A manufacturing plant has 7 different components that must pass through 7 specialized workstations.

Each component follows a specific processing route defined as (Workstation, Processing duration) pairs,
where each pair indicates the workstation where the operation must occur and how long it will take.
The sequence of pairs shows the required order in which these processing steps must be completed.

Component processing sequences:
* C1 follows: (W6, 7) → (W1, 1) → (W7, 10) → (W4, 1) → (W2, 7) → (W3, 2) → (W5, 5)
* C2 follows: (W2, 1) → (W6, 4) → (W3, 1) → (W7, 1) → (W1, 7) → (W5, 9) → (W4, 1)
* C3 follows: (W2, 1) → (W1, 9) → (W5, 10) → (W7, 7) → (W6, 2) → (W4, 9) → (W3, 3)
* C4 follows: (W2, 4) → (W7, 7) → (W4, 1) → (W5, 10) → (W6, 5) → (W1, 1) → (W3, 10)
* C5 follows: (W3, 10) → (W6, 9) → (W7, 2) → (W5, 5) → (W4, 2) → (W2, 2) → (W1, 5)
* C6 follows: (W1, 4) → (W6, 7) → (W2, 9) → (W5, 9) → (W4, 2) → (W7, 9) → (W3, 2)
* C7 follows: (W6, 9) → (W4, 6) → (W1, 3) → (W7, 7) → (W2, 5) → (W5, 7) → (W3, 2)

Each processing operation must run without interruption once initiated,
and each workstation can only handle one component operation at any given time.
The goal is to schedule all component operations across the workstations
to minimize the total production time for completing all components.
